editorial:
Imagine you are a doctor who sees something so weird and scary that it sticks in your head forever. That is exactly what happens to Rose. After a patient does something crazy right in front of her, Rose starts seeing people with creepy, frozen smiles on their faces. You will feel her panic as she tries to figure out if she is losing her mind or if something evil is actually following her. The movie does a great job of making you feel uneasy because you never know when a jump scare is coming, and the vibe is just plain spooky from start to finish.

Sosie Bacon gives a great performance that makes you really care about her struggle. The pacing is quick, though some of the scares feel a bit familiar if you watch a lot of horror. Still, the twists keep you guessing. If you want the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the creepy details in the background. You could also rent it on Apple TV for a movie night with friends. It is a perfect pick for anyone who likes a movie that keeps them on edge.
endingExplained: Rose tries to stop the curse by killing the monster in her mind, but she fails. In the final scene, the monster takes over her body and makes her kill her ex-boyfriend. The curse then passes to the boyfriend's sister, who sees Rose smiling at her. This means the cycle starts all over again with a new victim. There is no happy ending; the evil entity simply found a new person to haunt.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves jump scares and psychological thrillers.
